title: Capacity Eviction and Soft Preemption Guidelines
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This runbook defines the policies, decision heuristics, telemetry thresholds, operational tooling, and step-by-step procedures for executing soft preemption and tenant eviction actions in the Redwood inference fleet. The goal is to preserve cluster and SLO stability while minimizing customer impact and ensuring clear post-incident evidence for RCA. This document covers: SLO-aware preemption logic, capacity scoring, graceful eviction flow, automated vs. manual actions, communication playbook, and post-action reviews.

Audience:
- SRE on-call engineers
- Capacity planners
- Product engineers owning model tenants
- Solutions/Support for customer-facing communications

Principles and intent:
- Prioritize SLO preservation: prefer preemption patterns that protect high-sensitivity SLOs and latency tail guarantees.
- Minimize user-visible errors: prefer soft preemption (throttling / degraded tier) before hard termination.
- Deterministic, auditable decisions: all preemption actions must be recorded to the capacity ledger with rationale and telemetry snapshots.
- Bias for automated hedges with explicit human override: automated controllers should act quickly for well-understood signals; humans intervene for ambiguous cases and cross-tenant disputes.

Key definitions:
- Soft preemption: temporary admission control changes (reduction in qps share, introduction of token-priority throttles, routing to slower model variant) that reduce tenant resource consumption without terminating running inference processes.
- Eviction (hard preemption): forcibly terminating warm pools or reclaiming GPU allocation from a tenant to free capacity; used as last resort.
- Tenant priority classes: {gold, standard, trial, system}. Gold has SLA-backed latency SLOs and eviction protections.

SLO and error budget considerations:
- Each tenant is associated with SLO attributes: latency_p50, latency_p95, availability_pct.
- Eviction risk score = weighted_sum(remaining_error_budget_pct * -1, current_burn_rate, historical_violation_count, tenant_priority_penalty).
- Thresholds (example):
  - If error_budget_remaining < 5% AND burn_rate > 4x baseline => candidate for preemption if cluster headroom < 8%
  - If p95 tail latency increases by > 40% for > 5m and cluster pressure is > 85% => trigger soft preemption policy evaluation

Telemetry and alerts (examples):
- Prometheus rules (example expressions):
  - High cluster pressure: sum(gpu_utilization_percent) / count(gpu_instances) > 0.85 for 5m
  - SLO burn acceleration: tenant_error_budget_burn_rate > 4 for 3m
  - Preemption candidate signal: tenant_request_queue_length > queue_limit AND tenant_latency_p95 > slo_p95 * 1.4 for 2m

Automated controllers and safe-guards:
- Capacity Arbiter (automation): evaluates preemption candidates every 30s, scores them, and executes soft preemption policies automatically when score > 75 and cluster headroom < 6%.
- Human confirmation required for hard eviction: automated system may schedule an eviction but must wait for on-call approval (Slack flow + on-call approval button) unless an emergency mode is manually enabled by SRE lead.
- Rate-limit auto-actions: no more than 1 automated hard eviction per cluster per 6h; soft preemptions limited to 3 per tenant per 24h.

Soft preemption options (in order of preference):
1) Throttle low-priority tokens (token-priority admission control).
2) Switch tenant to a compatible lower-cost model variant (e.g., quantized 8-bit variant) with explicit model-fidelity tag and monitored quality regression.
3) Reduce concurrency / session affinity for tenant to reduce warm pool size.
4) Route new requests to a spillover region with lower latency guarantees (if available).

Hard eviction triggers (only after soft options exhausted and explicit approval):
- Active, long-running host-level OOM cascade tied to tenant model and no mitigation possible within 10 minutes.
- Legal/compliance takedown requests (escalate to Security & Legal).
- Cluster capacity protection: predicted capacity deficit > 15% for next 30 minutes and no alternate capacity routes.

Decision matrix (simplified):
| Signal | Cluster Headroom | Automation Allowed? | Action Priority | Notes |
|--------|------------------|---------------------|-----------------|-------|
| High SLO burn rate | <6% | Yes (soft only) | 1 | Run Capacity Arbiter score; prefer token throttles |
| Sustained p95 spike | 6-12% | Yes | 2 | Try variant switch, session drain |
| Predicted 30m deficit | <5% | Manual recommended | 3 | Human to validate traffic forecasts |
| OOM cascade | Any | Manual required | 0 | Emergency eviction after approval |

Operational runbook: step-by-step
1) Detect: alert fires for cluster_pressure OR tenant_preemption_candidate.
2) Triage (0-5m):
   - Confirm signals: check Grafana dashboards for cluster headroom, per-tenant QPS, warm pool sizes, and current SLO burn dashboards.
   - Run `rctl capacity score --tenant <tenant_id> --window 5m` to fetch current capacity score and preemption rationale.
3) Automated path (if Capacity Arbiter action already executed):
   - Inspect the arbiter log: `rctl arbiter status --cluster <cluster>`
   - Validate soft preemption effects in metrics (drop in QPS, latency changes) for 2m.
   - If metrics degrade for critical tenants, roll back the arbiter action: `rctl arbiter rollback --action-id <id>` and escalate to SRE lead.
4) Manual preemption (recommended when automation not allowed):
   - Initiate soft preemption policy: `rctl preempt soft --tenant <tenant_id> --policy token-throttle --max-drop 30`
   - Monitor effect for 3m. If no improvement, attempt model variant switch: `rctl preempt soft --tenant <tenant_id> --policy variant-switch --target-model <model-id-quant8>`
   - Notify product owner and support via the incident Slack channel with the action summary template (see Communications section below).
5) Hard eviction (CRITICAL step; human approval required):
   - Open an approval thread: tag oncall and SRE lead.
   - Run `rctl preempt hard --tenant <tenant_id> --evict-gpus 2 --force` after approval and document the approval in the ticket.
   - Immediately capture a full telemetry snapshot: `rctl snapshot --cluster <cluster> --tenants <list>` and attach to ticket.

Communication template (for Slack/email to stakeholders):
- Subject: [Preemption] Cluster <cluster> — Soft preemption applied to <tenant_id> — reason: <brief reason>
- Body:
  - Time: <UTC time>
  - Action: <soft_preempt|hard_evict>
  - Rationale: <short description linking alerts and score>
  - Expected impact: <approx % QPS reduction or downtime window>
  - Owner: <SRE on-call name>
  - Follow-up: link to ticket and expected RCA date

Tooling snippets and examples:
- Capacity score JSON (example CLI output):
  {
    "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
    "score": "82",
    "factors": ["high_burn:50","queue_pressure:20","priority_penalty:12"],
    "recommended_action": "token_throttle"
  }
- Example rctl commands:
  - rctl preempt soft --tenant tenant-123 --policy token-throttle --max-drop 25 --reason "cluster pressure spike"
  - rctl arbiter status --cluster inference-us-west-2
  - rctl preempt hard --tenant tenant-123 --evict-gpus 1 --reason "emergency capacity"

Logging and evidence collection requirements:
- Every preemption action must emit a capacity_ledger entry with fields: action_id, tenant_id, cluster, action_type, rationale, oncall, approval_ids (if applicable), telemetry_snapshot_link.
- Ensure the snapshot includes: process lists for affected nodes, top GPU memory consumers, kernel OOM logs, per-tenant request traces for the last 10m, and SLO burn metrics.

Post-action review checklist (within 48h):
- Did the action preserve cluster SLOs? (compare pre/post p95 and availability)
- Was the chosen action minimal-impact? (could a softer action have been used?)
- Was the tenant priority classification correct?
- Were automation safeguards respected (rate limits, approvals)?
- Create follow-up tasks (capacity expansion, model optimization, quota negotiation) and assign owners.

Escalation and dispute resolution:
- If a tenant or product owner disputes eviction, open a rapid arbitration with: SRE lead, product owner, account manager. Decisions should be recorded in the capacity ledger.
- For compliance/legal takedown requests, escalate immediately to Security & Legal and follow the restricted data handling playbook.

Capacity planning and preventative measures (long-term):
- Maintain 12% cluster headroom target for inference clusters serving gold tenants; use predictive heuristics to provision proactively.
- Quarterly audits of tenant priority and usage patterns; reclassify if sustained overcommit observed.
- Run simulated eviction rehearsals in the chaos lab quarterly to validate rollback and communication paths.

Metrics to report monthly to product and finance:
- Number of soft preemptions by tenant class and cluster.
- Number of hard evictions and justification.
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for preemption events.
- % of preemptions initiated by automation vs. human.

RCA and evidence standards:
- For every hard eviction, produce an RCA with timeline, decision rationale, raw telemetry, and corrective actions attached. Follow the incident review template: include hypothesis, reproducer steps (if applicable), and capacity remediation plan.

Appendix A — Example Prometheus alert YAML:
ALERT CapacityHighPressure
  IF sum(gpu_utilization_percent) / count(gpu_instances) > 0.85
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS {
    summary = "Inference cluster high GPU pressure",
    runbook = "confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/capacity-eviction-and-soft-preemption-guidelines-2026"
  }

Appendix B — Quick checklist for on-call (one-pager):
- Validate alert and cluster headroom.
- Run capacity score for top 5 tenants.
- Apply token throttles (soft) where safe.
- Notify product owners for affected tenants.
- If hard eviction needed: obtain approval, snapshot telemetry, perform eviction, document approval.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: eng-sre capacity working group
- Review cadence: 6 months or after any hard eviction RCA
- Amendments: record minor policy changes in the capacity_ledger and link them back to this page.
